correctness.rationale: For fixed N, Hill one is exactly N divided by the N-th root of the integer product P, Hill two exactly N^2/C. Writing counts as one plus a partition of t=N-k, Karamata for strictly convex square and x log x excludes reversal for every comparable pair, uniformly in unbounded k. The complete partition counts 1,1,2,3,5,7,11,15 through t=7 and six explicit incomparable pair comparisons leave precisely one strict opposite-sign pair at t=7. The independent extracted checker reproduces the exact integer comparisons and tests finite k as redundancy; infinity in k is handled analytically.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Rényi/Hill entire-order comparisons and majorization are broader mathematical frameworks; they do not state or automatically imply which first integer partition pair causes a strict order-one/order-two reversal. The related multi-crossing four-species result concerns two changes of ranking as the diversity order varies, not this first two-index census cutoff.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The 20-individual result requires agreement of two other diversity orders and is silent about simple order-one/order-two discordance at N=k+7; the eight-excess result compares inverse Simpson to dominance of the most common species; Shannon–Brillouin and Simpson–rarefaction use different indices. Generic majorization restricts reversals to incomparable abundance partitions but does not classify their first sign disagreement. Thus none of these statements logically covers the claimed universal first strict pair.

originality.rationale: Targeted published-claim comparisons and close primary texts identify definitions and index discordances but no seven-excess threshold or exact unique first pair with both richness and census fixed. The universal threshold and its finite-partition certificate are not immediate corollaries of their generic majorization statements; source-search and indexing limits remain. The three closest indexed source results were also read in full: one reports the stricter three-index predicate, one compares Berger–Parker and Simpson rather than Shannon and Simpson, and one bounds numbers of Hill-order crossings without quantifying the integer census.
residual_risks: An unindexed historical integer-partition or entropy-majorization census table might contain the same minimal witness under different nomenclature.
The work does not prove that no unpublished or unindexed exhaustive enumeration exists; searches do not prove absolute historical priority.

value.rationale: The problem compares two canonical and routinely co-reported effective biodiversity indices under identical integer-census and richness controls. The universal richness-adjusted first-disagreement threshold, its exact uniqueness and the primitive three-species witness characterize a natural identifiability boundary for interpreting conflicting index rankings, rather than merely computing an arbitrary small example. It does not assert empirical superiority of an index or sampling accuracy.
